questions.question: During October — November, the apparent movement of sun is towards the _____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**South.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The** apparent movement** of the **sun **during** October and November** is towards the** South.**
 
• This is because during these months, the **Earth is tilted away from the sun** in the **Northern Hemisphere **and **towards the sun** in the **Southern Hemisphere.**
 
• As a result, the sun appears to move towards the South, and the **days become shorter** in the Northern Hemisphere and** longer** in the Southern Hemisphere.
 
• This phenomenon is known as the **winter solstice** and occurs around** December 21st **in the Northern Hemisphere and** June 21st** in the Southern Hemisphere.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **movement of the sun** is caused by the** Earth's rotation on its axis **and its **revolution **around the sun.
 
• The Earth's axis is tilted at an** angle of 23.5 degrees **relative to its orbit around the sun, which** causes the seasons.**
 
• During the **winter solstice**, the tilt of the Earth's axis is at its **maximum,** causing the** least amount of daylight** in the Northern Hemisphere and the **most amount of daylight** in the Southern Hemisphere.
 
• The opposite occurs during the **summer solstice,** which happens around** June 21st** in the Northern Hemisphere and** December 21st** in the Southern Hemisphere.
 
• During the **equinoxes**, which occur around **March 20th and September 22nd, **the tilt of the Earth's axis is perpendicular to the sun, causing **equal amounts of daylight and darkness** all over the world.

questions.question: What is the characteristic of isotopes?

• **Isotopes** have the **same atomic number **but **different mass numbers.**
 
• Isotopes are variants of a **chemical element **that have the** same number of protons** in their atomic nuclei but **different numbers of neutrons.**

• Isotopes are commonly used in** scientific research, medical diagnosis, and treatment**, as well as in industrial and environmental applications.

• **Goa** is a state in western India, known for its **beaches, nightlife, and rich culture**.
 
 
• Apart from Dhangar dance, Goa is also known for its folk dance forms like **Fugdi, Goff, and Kunbi dance.**

questions.question: Which of the following ocean is the smallest in the world?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Arctic Ocean.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Arctic Ocean** is the **smallest ocean** in the world in terms of area, covering approximately **14.05 million square kilometers.**
 
• The Arctic Ocean is located in the northern part of the Earth and is surrounded by the northern coasts of **North America, Europe, and Asia.**
 
• The Arctic Ocean is** covered with ice **for most of the year, making it difficult to navigate.
 
• The Arctic Ocean is home to a diverse range of** marine life, including polar bears, walruses,** and various species of whales and fish.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The** Pacific Ocean** is the** largest ocean **in the world, covering approximately** 165.2 million square kilometers.**
 
• The** Indian Ocean** is the **third largest ocean** in the world, covering approximately **70.6 million square kilometers.**
 
• The **Atlantic Ocean** is the** second largest ocean** in the world, covering approximately **76.8 million square kilometers.**

questions.question: Bastar Dussehra is a famous festival of ______ state of India.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chhattisgarh.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bastar Dussehra** is a famous festival celebrated in the state of **Chhattisgarh, India**.
 
• It is celebrated for** 75 days **and is one of the longest festivals in India.
 
• The festival marks the **victory of Lord Ram over Ravana **and is celebrated by the local tribes of Bastar.
 
• The festival is known for its **unique cultural practices **such as the use of **chariots and wooden idols **during the procession.
 
• The festival also features** traditional dance forms and music **performances.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Manipur **is known for its **Yaoshang festival,** which is celebrated in the month of **March.**
 
• **Bihar **is known for its **Chhath Puja, **which is celebrated in the month of **November.**
 
• **Arunachal Pradesh **is known for its **Losar festival**, which is celebrated by the **Monpa tribe** in the month of February.
 
• **Chhattisgarh** is also known for its other festivals such as **Navakhana, Madai, and Pola**.

questions.question: Who among the following was awarded the prestigious title of 'Nrityacharya' conferred by the Maharaja of Manipur?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Guru Bipin Singh.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Guru Bipin Singh** was awarded the prestigious title of** 'Nrityacharya'** by the **Maharaja of Manipur.**
 
• Guru Bipin Singh was a renowned **Indian classical dancer, choreographer, and teacher.**
 
• He was one of the pioneers of **Manipuri dance** in India.
 
• He founded the **Manipuri Nartanalaya in 1952, **which became a hub for the promotion and propagation of **Manipuri dance and culture.**
 
• Guru Bipin Singh was also awarded the** Padma Shri in 1977** for his contributions to the field of dance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rukmini Devi** was a well-known Indian classical **dancer and choreographer** who is credited with reviving and popularizing Bharatanatyam.
 
• **Uday Shankar **was a legendary **Indian dancer and choreographer** who is known for his pioneering work in fusing Indian classical dance with Western ballet.
 
• **Guru Kelucharan Mohapatra** was a celebrated **Odissi dancer and guru** who is considered one of the pioneers of the Odissi revival.
